Homes & housing 1

Talk about where you live in Thai. This first part of Homes & housing covers the options — a บ้านเดี่ยว (detached house), บ้านแฝด (semi-detached), ตึกแถว (shophouse), คอนโด (condo), อพาร์ตเมนต์ (apartment) or หอพัก (dorm), renting versus buying — and the building itself: ชั้น (floors), the ดาดฟ้า (roof deck), หลังคา (roof), ประตูรั้ว (gate), กำแพง (wall) and สนามหญ้า (lawn). All 16 sentences come with native-speed audio, English translations and word-by-word notes, so the housing vocabulary sticks by ear.

16 sentences · Click each sentence to reveal Thai, English, and notes

A ตึกแถว is a narrow multi-storey shophouse — a shop or workshop on the ground floor with living space above — lining the streets of most Thai towns.

Thai has three words where English just says 'flat': คอนโด (condo) are units you buy, อพาร์ตเมนต์ (apartments) are rented buildings, and แฟลต (flats) are older, cheaper walk-ups.
